coverage.r1: Whole file read in order. 05:05-24:00 and 47:00-1:07:03 are largely Latin-transliterated on Medi's side; he renders ك as q throughout (qasar=kasar, qasat=kasat) and drops ق/ع (عطلوا=2atalu at 26:47/27:15, ami=3ammi 06:05, بتدري=bte2dari 34:41) - all S4, not written. Not written (S4/S5/self-fix): 01:24 بتيت (unclear word he asked about, Amal 'it doesn't go'); 02:04 ما تفي for مطفي; 05:05 'هلات إلى 12' vs chat talaat illa tult (chat transcribes what he said right); 06:05 ami/amoy -> عمي (dropped ع); 14:57 كسروا->انكسروا and 17:13 اكسرو->ما تكسرو (self-fixed before she spoke); 27:52 & 28:13 كسا for كسر (root-letter slip, she echoed كسر); 41:43 بنغير self-doubt; 43:53 خيارات = garbled غيرتي; 44:12 شعرها->شعرك self-fix; 48:51 matitsawri self-fix; 51:58-52:19 sawarna he asked, first form was right; 58:37 'Zakarini'/'Less e' unclear, her chat gives both zakkerni and zakkrini; 1:03:08 Asma vs Asmaa = F2 vowel length. 16:18-16:35 Amal repeats تكسري without b- while chat has btekser - ambiguous, not written. 27:25 'Fat' is his English placeholder for fought while checking meaning, not counted as tier 3. No swapped speaker labels noticed. English-only stretches: 07:00-07:50 (leave/go discussion), 21:44-24:00 (fi discussion), 36:00-36:50, 1:03:26-1:05:00 (Farsi/shukr chat).
coverage.r2: Latin-transliterated stretches: 06:05-11:46 (Kevin/uncle story, break drill start), 18:14-23:39 (teeth/cups/did-anything-break), 48:51-1:04:18 (photograph drill end, remind/remember drill) - Arabic there is engine-Latin, so vowel-level fixes (kasat/kasarat, zakkerni/zakarini) rest on the Latin. Garbled Medi lines I could not defend and left out: [01:24] 'بتيت' (asked if it works for يوم; she said it doesn't go - meaning unclear), [01:58] 'شو كما ما مرا', [04:42] 'آه هلا قلبك', [05:05] 'هلات إلى 12' (chat 'talaat illa tult' - could be a right answer mis-transcribed), [10:48] 'haketni bare', [43:53] 'خيارات' (she prompted 'you changed' -> he then said غيرتي; likely a mishearing of his غيرت), [52:30]/[54:23] 'kamamana', [55:46] 'ana nafu', [58:00] 'maqtarakhar'. Pronunciation left out per S4: مطفي said as 'ما تفي' (02:04), 'ami' for عمي (06:05), 'metakhri' (06:46), كسا for كسر (27:52, 28:13 - root-letter slip), 'طيار'/'طيرنا' for غيّر (30:17, 31:39 - engine spelling), كندكتك for كندرتك (38:36), شعرك heard by Amal as شهر (44:12-44:23 - she asked 'What's hair?' but he had said شعرك; dropped ع), khubas for خبز (59:09), 'fahis' for حاسس (1:05:15), Asma vs Asmaa vowel length (1:03:08). [35:34] he said in English 'Program shift feminine' and Amal fixed 'Program is masculine' before any Arabic verb was uttered - not a row. [41:58] 'بوتنا' vs chat '5u66atna' is written as a low vocab-B because Amal said Perfect. [47:37] transcript 'تصوري' vs chat 'tetsawwari' - she said ممتاز aloud, so likely engine dropped a ت; not a row. [53:33-54:54] transcript shows 'bisawar' but Amal says on record he said يصور without b - not a row.

r3_note: Chat lines in this lesson are Amal typing EVERY target sentence 1-4 min after the fact, not only fixes; a chat line alone is weak evidence unless she also reacted aloud. Latin stretches (08:27-11:46, 18:14-24:00, 49:40-56:00, 1:00-1:06) are engine-garbled, so dropped b-/t- prefixes there may be engine drops - those rows are kept as B with low confidence. D2 and D21 are the same slip (ma tekseri without -ih); kept once as D2. Possible misses NOT in the disputes and not added because I cannot see the agreed list: 31:21 'احنا ان لازم' -> Amal 'we just should, not should have' (looks like كان لازم, B16) and 31:39 'طيرنا' -> Amal 'should change. present. مضارع' (past after لازم, B2/B5); 1:00:02 'Zakaretik' for 'I reminded him' (wrong object pronoun, D4). Merger should check these are covered by agreed rows.

rows.medi_said: أناا بدأت شغلي على تسعة ونص.
rows.right: من وين = from where (an answer to where, e.g. كنت في محل)

rows.english: Where are you working from today?
rows.r3_why: Explicit signal in the transcript, but it is his understanding of her question word that failed, so mode listening, tier 0.

rows.why: Clock time needs el-saa3a + number, not 3ala; Amal only redirected the question (min wain) and let the time phrase pass.

rows.why: He offered معروف / مرفوف for 'ground (meat)'; the word is مفروم, which Amal supplied; sheet: 'ground beef | La7meh mafrumeh | لحمة مفرومة'.

He produced مفروم then offered the feminine مفرومة after masculine لحم عجل; she answered with the masculine مفروم. Low: her sheet's own entry is feminine (لحمة مفرومة), so he may have been echoing the sheet, and his second try reads like a question she settled.
rows.r3_why: Transcript shows him ending on مفرومة and her replying مفروم إيه - a gender pick on the adjective (A8); weak but real, kept low.

rows.amal_said: Yeah, we don't say that yesterday. Just yesterday is its own...

Telling what his cousin did yesterday he said 'aji' (not the he-form); she recast to أجا (sheet 'he came | huwwe aja | هو إجا').
'Came to my house' takes 3ala/3and, not min (from); Amal said no and gave أجا على, then أجا عندي (06:43).

rows.medi_said: Aja andi wu rah bad, um, metakhri.

rows.r3_why: Her repeat-and-rephrase is a real signal that he did not follow; his production is unreadable, so kept low as a listening row.

rows.chat: e7na benfaddel enno inti ma tekserih
rows.why: After بنفضل انه the verb is bare (ma tekseri), he kept the b- (ما بتكسري); Amal recast without b- and typed the full sentence.

rows.chat: e7na benfaddel enno inti ma tekserih
rows.why: 'We prefer that you don't break IT' - his ما تكسري has no object ending; her drawn-out ما تكسرييي at 12:54 and her typed ma tekserih add -ih. Medium: aloud at 12:45 she herself modelled ما تكسري, so he was echoing her.

rows.r3_why: Real missing object pronoun, fixed in chat (and hinted aloud). Same slip as D21 - kept once here at his first line.

rows.why: 'I broke it' - he said كسرتوا (the you-plural / -u ending); she recast كسرته and typed KAsarto, adding 'anything to make the verb so easy and shorter'; he repeated كسرتوا.
'Why did THEY break them' needs the plural past kasaru-hom; he said kasar-hom (he broke them); Amal said mm-hmm aloud but typed the plural.
'What broke them' is transitive kasar; he used the get-broken form انكسر with an object; Amal recast كسرهم and typed it.
'Since when' needs من امتى; transcript shows bare امتى (when) and she said Perfect, so a let-pass - her typed min aimta is her routine target sentence, not a fix. Low: من may be an engine drop.

rows.amal_said: تكسري. What's plural of أشي إشي؟ / تكسري أشياء.

rows.medi_said: Is it اكسرو؟ / اكسرو. اكسرو؟ Oh, ما تكسرو.
